rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing – use of algorithmic devices by landlords
rules.requirement: Proposed ordinance would make it unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device (software that uses nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels) to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. Each month a violation continues, and each property where the device is used, is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property in the City of San Diego using software or products that perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels.
rules.exemptions: Does not cover software used to publish reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or from information available to the general public that does not recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for future leases or renewals; or software used to establish rental rates or income limits under local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.penalty: A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation in a civil action against a landlord; a prevailing tenant recovers costs and reasonable attorney's fees. Each month a violation continues and each residential rental property is a separate violation.
rules.quoted_span: (b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This Ordinance will take effect and be in force on the thirtieth day from and after its final passage.
rules.interaction_text: The remedies under section 98.1104 are cumulative and are in addition to any other remedies in this Division or at law, statute, or ordinance.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing – sale and licensing of algorithmic devices
rules.requirement: Proposed ordinance would make it unlawful for any person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.
rules.coverage_text: Persons selling, licensing, or providing to landlords software or products that use nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Does not cover software used to publish reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or from information available to the general public that does not recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for future leases or renewals; or software used to establish rental rates or income limits under local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.quoted_span: (a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This Ordinance will take effect and be in force on the thirtieth day from and after its final passage.
